newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strategie Grains lowers EU '97 grain crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: Strategie Grains lowers EU '97 grain crop forecast.

text.p: French grain analyst Strategie Grains said on Tuesday it had revised down its forecast for 1997 European Union grain output to 199.8 million tonnes from last month's target of 201.6 million.
This would represent a decline of two percent from the 203.4 million tonnes produced in 1996.
In its July report Strategie Grains put the 1997 soft wheat crop at 89 million tonnes against 89.9 million tonnes last month and 90.9 million in 1996.
It predicted a barley crop of 51.1 million tonnes against 51.8 million forecast last month and 51.7 million last year.
The maize crop was forecast at 34.1 million tonnes against 34.3 million last month and 34.2 million last year.
The new estimate assumed an average grain yield of 5.3 tonnes per hectare against 5.4 tonnes last month and 5.5 tonnes last year.
Strategie Grains linked the downward revision to problems caused by excess moisture levels following heavy rain in late June and early July.
"The yield potential that would have increased over a month without these problems caused by excess rain remains at last month's level for wheat but slightly declines for barley," it said.
Strategie Grains predicted an average soft wheat yield of 6.4 tonnes per hectare, unchanged from last month but down three percent over last year.
But it revised downwards its estimate for barley yields to 4.3 tonnes from 4.4 tonnes last month and 4.5 tonnes last year.
The maize yield was put at 8.2 tonnes against 8.18 tonnes last month and 8.3 tonnes last year.
The rain initially brought relief to thirsty crops in northern Europe, but excess moisture led to outbreaks of disease in France and Britain.
Strategie Grains cautioned that plants had not reached the crucial maturing stage where yields could sustain severe losses.
In southern Europe the rain that stopped the harvest in its tracks led to unwanted germination in Italy, Spain and southern France.
